subject: problematic mixing with constraint on transformed parameter

messages.author: 2430f2828c808219
messages.subject: problematic mixing with constraint on transformed parameter
parts:
Hi all

Can someone please explain the following behaviour by the sampler in rstan 2.7 run on R 3.2.2.  It does not seem right but I am likely ignorant about the underlying mechanics.

I am predicting a response y given a mean of alpha[1] + alpha[2]*x and sd of sigma.  I am also specifying a variable beta in the transformed parameter block that is derived from an estimated parameter gamma.  Simplified code is attached.  Chain traces and n_eff of alpha are much lower when beta is truncated between 0 and 1 (I am doing this in a larger model for a specific reason), and the model arguably isn't converging when run longer.  But importantly gamma never appears in the model block so shouldn't lp__ be driven by y?...

Why is a transformed parameter that doesn't influence any parameter in the model block affecting the sampler's performance for the alpha parameters?  And is there a way to control the sampler to mitigate this issue, i.e. estimate alpha's irrespective of gamma? 

Thanks for the help,
Andrew

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problematic mixing with constraint on transformed parameter
parts:
Ah, but it does influence a parameter. If the transformed parameter
constraints are violated, the whole sample is rejected.

These assignments are not consistent in their constraints:

parameters {
real gamma[Ncon];

transformed parameters {

real<lower=0,upper=1> beta[N]; //alpha sampled well when truncation is removed


beta[i] <- gamma[consumer[i]];

The problem is that gamma can be outside of [0, 1]. Whenver that
happens, you reject.

Either constrain gamma or unconstrain beta. Or, do an inverse-logit
transform to turn the unconstrained gamma into a probability in [0, 1].

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problematic mixing with constraint on transformed parameter
parts:
I see what you mean --- alpha and gamma are disconnected in the model.

The constraint on beta will constrain gamma by rejection. Without
the constraint, given that there's no prior on gamma, the posterior
is improper and all bets are off. With the constraint, the HMC
sampler will have a hard time and may not even be randomly initializable.

In any case, you need to constrain gamma to [0, 1], at which point the
posterior will be proper and you'll be sampling from the model you
have defined.

- Bob


data{
int<lower=1> N;
int<lower=1> Ncon;
int<lower=1> Nchemsites;
int<lower=1> consumer[N];
real x[Nchemsites];
real y[Nchemsites];
}
parameters{
real<lower=0,upper=30> sigma;
real alpha[2];

real gamma[Ncon];
}
transformed parameters{
real<lower=0,upper=1> beta[N]; //alpha sampled well when truncation is removed

real mu[Nchemsites];
for (i in 1:Nchemsites)
mu[i] <- alpha[1] + alpha[2]*x[i];
for (i in 1:N)

model{
alpha ~ normal(0,10);
y ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}

- Bob
